scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: The common-cause hypothesis that Ki-67, TK1, CDK1, and biosynthetic genes co-vary with active cell-cycle state is well established and biologically coherent. It appropriately avoids claiming that TK1 directly regulates Ki-67.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: TK1 was connected to S-phase DNA synthesis, CDK1 to the broader S/G2/M program, and ribosomal genes to the increased biosynthetic activity of proliferating cells. These features were unified mainly as parallel readouts of cycling state, without detailed transitions explaining regulation of Ki-67 abundance. No formal ceiling was applied, although the broad common-state mechanism limits mechanistic resolution.
